text:
alex: heads-up — CI eval runner is flaky on the structured-funcall suite, reproduced locally. test: `structured-funcall/parity-replay` failing intermittently with mismatched tool call args between fp16 and q8 models.

maya: ugh. failing in which stage? model conversion, quantized runtime, or the runner harness?

alex: mismatch occurs at the runner comparator after replay. replayed function calls look different: arg ordering and an extra null. see snippet from the test harness log:

```
EXPECTED: {"tool":"weather","args":{"city":"sf","units":"metric"}}
ACTUAL:   {"tool":"weather","args":{"units":"metric","city":"sf", "locale": null}}
```

samir: that extra `locale: null` smells like defaulting in the quantized model's tokenizer postprocessing. but ordering shouldn't matter for JSON equality. is comparator doing strict string compare?

alex: yes — bad assumption on my part. comparator does naive json.dumps on both outputs and compares strings for speed. it failed to normalize key order and ignored null semantics.

maya: we should fail tests only on semantic diffs. quick fix: use canonical JSON compare (sorted keys + drop nulls when allowed by schema). but we also need to be careful for arrays where order is significant.

ev an: +1 for schema-aware diffs. Also saw intermittent CI timeouts when the runner tries to rehydrate KV cache during replay on q8b — may be unrelated but started same day.

alex: created a local patch: comparator now does `json.loads` then run `jsonschema` validation against expected schema, prune keys with `nullable` allowed if value is null, then deep-compare. patch passes locally for 12/15 runs. still failing 3 times with a new error: `FuncCallReplayError: missing tool 'weather' in call history` on quantized run only.

ci-bot: CI pipeline `evals/structured-funcall` failed 3/7 jobs — see https://ci.internal/redwood/ev/4821 for logs :rotating_light:.

samir: missing tool in call history suggests the model didn't emit the tool call tokenization exactly. Could be a streaming chunk reassembly bug in q8 path (we patched that recently). Can you paste the raw token traces from failing run?

alex: here are the token traces (trimmed):

```
# fp16 success (tokens near end)
...  5023: "(tool_call)"
...  5024: "{"
...  5025: "\"tool\""
...  5026: ":"
...  5027: "\"weather\""
...  5028: "}"

# q8b fail (tokens split)
...  5000: "(tool_call)"
...  5001: "{\"tool\":\"wea"
...  5002: "ther\",\"args\""
...  5003: ":{\"city\":\"sf\"}"
...  5004: "}"
```

maya: looks like token chunking merged string fragments differently; the runner's tokenizer-joiner expects tokens to correspond to JSON atomic chunks. If a token splits a multi-byte sequence, our reassembler might fail to detect the boundary.

samir: I can reproduce the split behavior using the q8b tokenizer with a forced chunk size. reassembler code currently assumes tokens are valid UTF-8 boundaries. in q8 encoding we sometimes encode subword parts that when concatenated produce JSON tokens across boundaries.

alex: propose three actions: 1) immediate test harness fix — canonical JSON compare + treat ordering-insensitive maps as such; 2) add reassembly sanity check that stitches token strings before parsing and asserts valid JSON; 3) add targeted fuzz tests to CI to cover chunk splits.

evan: agree. also suggest adding a metric to the dashboard for "replay-parity-pass-rate" by model/quantization, so we spot regressions early. product wants to know per-model brittleness.

maya: for the canonical compare patch, watch out for function call semantics where `null` can be semantically meaningful vs omitted. we need to consult the schema's `nullable` property. I'll add schema-aware pruning.

alex: implemented (1) as a small change in runner comparator, test PR: https://git.internal/redwood/pulls/9234 — passes on my laptop but CI still flaky. landing (1) will reduce noise though.

ci-bot: PR 9234 status: build queued -> running.

samir: for (2) I'll open a follow-up PR to the reassembler: detect partial JSON tokens and run a microconcat stage that merges adjacent token payloads until parsing succeeds or we reach a threshold. I'll add unit tests that replicate the q8 split traces.

alex: created an issue for (3): https://issues.internal/redwood/INF-1772 - will add a small corpus of fuzz cases and run them in CI nightly.

maya: one more operational ask — can we tag any future flaky job with metadata `eval-suite:structured-funcall` and `model:quantized` so the dashboard can filter? I can add that to the CI job wrapper.

evan: yes we can. I'll add tags and a dashboard panel.

qa-bot: nightly fuzz job scheduled. I'll report parity-pass-rate hourly to metrics store. :rocket:

alex: thanks all — next steps: land comparator patch, samir to PR reassembler, evan to tag jobs + dashboard, maya to add schema pruning tests. I'll follow up in this thread with CI results. :thumbsup:

maya: note for retrospective — runner should never rely on string equality for structured outputs. moving to schema-first diffs reduces many classes of flakes.

alex: agreed. small follow-up: keep an eye on latency delta when we add reassembly microconcat — avoid blocking streaming path. we'll prefer a best-effort reassembly in async path before failing replay.

samir: I'll benchmark reassembler changes locally and post numbers here.

alex: closing loop for now. leaving logs and token traces in the PR review.
